title: Temporal Equivalence Principle: A Proper-Time Domain Boundary in the Outer Solar System
abstract:
Adopting the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP) field framework established in the companion corpus, this paper tests an outer-solar-system realization: a localized proper-time domain boundary organizing detached trans-Neptunian residents and long-period comet transits about the same 60° sector of inertial sky. The two populations probe complementary secular and crossing responses.

The detached resident population clusters in perihelion longitude (R_ϖ = 0.332, conditioned-null p = 0.00735), and a Keplerian discovery-selection model retains a directional excess on the 52 class-1 objects within its stated visibility limits (p = 0.0092). In the transit population, the primary coordinate-level observable — spatial aphelion anisotropy computed directly from osculating elements with no three-leg reconstruction — leans toward the shared sector across both historical and modern eras (d_∥ = +0.110, p < 10⁻⁴ pre-2018; d_∥ = +0.0949, p = 0.00215 post-2017; Fisher-combined p = 1.8×10⁻⁶; full CometEls census d_∥ = +0.10, p = 2×10⁻³), remaining flat across all orbit-quality and arc-length strata. As a secondary, solver-sensitive observable, the CODE three-leg transit record carries a direction-dependent orbit-reconstruction rotation (p = 0.00295), retained after planetary-encounter and observing-leverage controls. Independent two-leg fits of raw Minor Planet Center astrometry for 585 pre-2018 comets reproduce catalogue rotations (ρ = +0.998) and retain the inbound-leg excess (p = 0.0370; CODE-overlap p = 0.00688), with no resolved in-cap energy excess. Under crossing-localized transport, the angular residual corresponds to an equivalent-time contrast of +4.9 yr; this is a model-conditioned conversion rather than a direct clock reading.

A ten-channel synthesis across six catalogue lineages gives S₁₀ = 186.2 at the resident axis, with conditional sky-area rank 0.0145 on the fixed observed catalogues. This measures directional convergence; it is not a global discovery probability. While the coordinate-level aphelion dipole persists unchanged in the post-2017 holdout, the estimator-dependent reconstruction channel reverses its declared-axis carrier and exhibits a displaced residual structure under short-arc solver absorption, restricting the simple stationary three-leg interpretation. Point-mass, tidal, drag and reduction explanations are tested through quantitative amplitude, localization and transfer-function controls. The canonical disformal benchmark specifies the required field excursion using actual conic entry and exit geometry; its source profile and full metric-to-observation response remain to be derived.

The results provide mutually reinforcing evidence for a shared direction-organized outer-system structure; its interpretation as an outer-system TEP domain boundary remains model-conditioned and testable through the prospective discoveries registered below. The registered prospective test predicts 59% of new detached objects in the cap, against a 42% characterized-footprint expectation, requiring approximately 123 discoveries for 95% power at a 1% test. This separates the present evidence from the next key validation.
